status: DONE. H_a, H_c, H_d HOLD; H_b FAILS. Pre-registered reading: a faint, calibrated, year-stable 1h probability of UP exists in the development data, but it is essentially one reversal feature. Research-only, hypothesis-generating, economically negligible. Nothing adopted; directional track only.
why: The user's long-term objective includes predicting DIRECTION with measurable, calibrated skill. Every earlier directional test asked an ECONOMIC question (an edge in returns) or a fit-free correlation question, and every one failed (E001, E002-E008, E011, E015, E017). E011 is the only fitted directional model: its pre-registered criterion required a return edge, which was zero. Its numbers also show, without any interval, a tiny probabilistic signal at 1h: Brier 0.2490 vs the base rate's 0.2499 (gain about 0.0009), ECE 0.005-0.007, and accuracy 1.5-2.5 points above naive in both periods. Three things were never established: whether that Brier gain is distinguishable from zero with an interval that respects hour-to-hour dependence; whether it is more than one reversal feature, since E011 had no simple directional baseline; and whether it holds year by year on a proper score. This answers exactly those questions and nothing else. It does NOT ask whether direction is useful: E011 and E015 already show it is not, at retail costs.
hypothesis: At 1h, E011's pre-defined reversal-family logistic produces out-of-sample probabilities of UP that beat a leak-free base rate on the Brier score with an interval excluding zero, in both periods; that beat a one-feature reversal logistic by a practically meaningful margin; that are calibrated; and that are stable across calendar years.
target: binary direction: y = 1 if the 1h return > 0 (UP). Reference = close at the cutoff (the reference candle's close); outcome = close of the candle opening at as_of + 1h (agent/research/labels, as E011). 1h only: E011 found 6h and 24h at chance, and E025 showed that longer overlapping targets need far more data for the same power.

data.permitted: The development period only, exploration (to 2023-12) and validation (2024-01 -> 2025-06-29), through model_test.build_frame -> load_bars(end=HOLDOUT.start).
data.never: No holdout candle (allow_holdout stays False; research/HOLDOUT_ACCESS.log must still not exist afterwards). No prospective or live outcome. Not the buffer.
data.category_scores: From the cached historical replay at the current scoring 0.2.0 (E017's). E011 used 0.1.0; the two are identical on every clean hour (E016) and differ only on the 9% of hours whose windows contain a gap.

features_and_leakage.model_inputs: E011's 'A_minus_volpct' list, unchanged: trend_score, momentum_score, volume_score, chart_pattern_score, tr_mean_14_rel, trades_rel_168h, taker_buy_share_1h, taker_buy_share_6h. It is E011's set A without vol_pct_720, a list E011 declared before it ran, chosen here for full coverage, since vol_pct_720 blanks about 24% of exploration hours after candle gaps. No new feature, no search.
features_and_leakage.leakage: Every input is point-in-time (perturbation-tested: tests/test_point_in_time.py, test_features_point_in_time.py). The walk-forward runner asserts on every fold that the last fitted row's label is realised before the first test cutoff (purge = horizon + 24h embargo; check_fold). Rows are restricted ONCE to hours where every candidate's inputs and the label exist, so all candidates are scored on identical rows.

validation_design: make_folds: expanding walk-forward, min_train_days 365, test blocks 90 days, embargo 24h, no calibration slice (E011's design, kept so the probabilities are E011's raw logistic, whose calibration is itself one of the questions). Exploration = out-of-sample hours before 2024-01-01; validation = 2024-01-01 -> 2025-06-29.

candidates.M_model: L2 logistic (agent/research/model_test.LogisticModel, C = 0.1, scaler fitted on each fold's training rows), the eight inputs above
candidates.F_one_feature: the same logistic on taker_buy_share_1h alone. It is the largest-magnitude, always-same-sign coefficient in E011's 1h model (tied with momentum_score), so it is the strongest simple reversal rule this record offers, which makes H_b conservative
candidates.B0_base_rate: agent/research/model_test.BaseRateModel: each fold's training-range share of UP hours, a leak-free constant (the proper-score baseline; E010 verified it)

metrics_reported_for_every_candidate_and: Brier score; Brier skill against B0 (1 - Brier/Brier_B0) and, descriptively, against the oracle base rate of the same rows; log loss
paired Brier differences with a 48h circular block bootstrap (agent/research/simple_baselines.paired_difference: 500 resamples), B0 - M and F - M
calibration: ECE, the reliability buckets with E013's rule, and the calibration intercept and slope; ECE is read cautiously
binary classification at the fixed threshold 0.5: accuracy against the naive majority of the same rows

economics, descriptive and never a criterion: the return edge (mean 1h return when p > 0.5 minus when p < 0.5) with a block-bootstrap interval, and the gross mean signed return per hour of 'long if p > 0.5 else short' against a 0.10% round trip
stability: Brier skill against B0 per calendar year 2018-2025
multiple_comparisons: One horizon, one model, two fixed baselines, so there is nothing to choose among. No other horizon, feature set, regulariser or threshold is run. Years are a pre-specified stability criterion, not a search; no subgroup is examined to rescue a failure.

hypotheses.H_a_skill_beyond_the_base_rate: In BOTH periods, Brier(B0) - Brier(M) > 0 and its paired 95% interval excludes zero.
hypotheses.H_b_more_than_one_reversal_feature: On validation, M's Brier skill against B0 is >= 1.10x F's AND the paired difference Brier(F) - Brier(M) has a 95% interval excluding zero (E020's two-part rule: statistically AND practically better).
hypotheses.H_c_calibrated: M's ECE <= 0.03 in both periods AND, on validation, every reliability bucket with >= 100 rows is within 0.05 of its observed frequency (E013's rule).
hypotheses.H_d_stable: M's Brier skill against B0 is positive in at least 6 of the 8 calendar years 2018-2025.

expectation_stated_in_advance: E011's figures, which this design will largely re-measure, suggest: a Brier gain of roughly 0.0009 (about 0.4%); H_a likely holds given ~45-56k hours; H_c likely holds (E011 ECE 0.005-0.007); H_d plausible (E011's accuracy was below naive in 2018); H_b genuinely uncertain. The return edge is expected to be about zero (E011). Written down so the result is read against what was already known, not as a discovery.
validation_wear: About ten directional experiments (E001-E011, E015, E017) and about 30 experiments in all have examined these periods, and E011 measured nearly this quantity on these rows. So the result is HYPOTHESIS-GENERATING ONLY: a pass re-describes a known faint signal with proper uncertainty, and a fail closes the probabilistic question on this data. It cannot be confirmed offline. The only clean confirmation would be a NEW, separately registered prospective direction shadow track, and that is the user's decision.

what_each_answer_means_decided_in_advanc.H_c_or_H_d_fails: Measurable but miscalibrated or unstable: recorded, not pursued without a new hypothesis.
what_each_answer_means_decided_in_advanc.in_every_case: The live BUY/HOLD/SELL signal, scoring 0.2.0, move_size_1h_v1, the shadow record, the checkpoints and the holdout are untouched. The two research tracks stay separate.

reading_by_the_pre_registered_consequenc: H_a HOLDS: the model's 1h P(UP) beats the leak-free base rate in both periods (Brier skill +0.0038 exploration, +0.0043 validation; both paired intervals exclude zero). E011's unexamined Brier gain is real, as expected in advance.

H_c HOLDS: calibrated (ECE 0.006 / 0.004, E013's bucket rule met). Exploration's calibration slope 1.22 says the raw logistic is slightly UNDER-confident there (probabilities too close to 0.5); validation's 1.02 is near ideal.
H_d HOLDS: skill positive in all 8 calendar years (2018 the weakest, +0.0017).

H_b FAILS on its statistical part: on validation the model's skill is 1.11x the one-feature rule's (the practical bar of 1.10x is met), but the paired difference [-0.00018, +0.00041] includes zero. In exploration the model IS clearly better than the one feature ([+0.00028, +0.00063]). By the rule as registered, H_b fails.

Consequence, decided in advance (H_a holds, H_b fails): the skill is essentially one reversal feature, taker-buy share, and the eight-input combination adds nothing practical on the most recent data. Any future directional track starts from the one-feature rule.

Economics (descriptive, never judged): the model's return edge is about zero in both periods. Trading the sign every hour grosses +0.0009% / +0.0069% per hour (model) and +0.0027% / +0.0134% (one feature), against a 0.10% round trip: 1-13% of the cost. The one feature's validation edge interval excludes zero (+0.024% [+0.007, +0.042]), but its exploration sign is negative (-0.020% [-0.043, +0.002]), so it is not stable. Measurable skill is not usefulness.

Size of the signal, plainly: about 0.4% better than the base rate on the Brier score, with Spearman rho about 0.05. It is the same faint short-horizon reversal the programme has seen since E002. Hypothesis-generating only (validation wear).

Nothing changes: the live BUY/HOLD/SELL signal, scoring 0.2.0, move_size_1h_v1, the checkpoints and the holdout are untouched, and nothing is combined with the move-size track. A prospective direction shadow track would be the only clean test, and it would be the user's decision.
